title: vacUUUm: cordless vacuum, concept to drawings
summary: A complete product-development cycle in Siemens NX: from user needs and requirements to subsystem design, exploded assemblies, production drawings and an ergonomic check in Tecnomatix.

cover.alt: Five color variants of the vacUUUm cordless vacuum

hero_media.alt: Exploded view of the vacuum's main subsystems
hero_media.caption: Exploded view of the main subsystems.

tldr: Turned user research into 11 measurable technical requirements, then into a modular architecture of seven subsystems.
Modeled every subsystem in Siemens NX — motor and impeller, cyclonic + HEPA filtration, 1 L bin, removable battery, charging base — with exploded views and drawings.
Checked the posture of right- and left-handed users in Tecnomatix before freezing the design.

sections.title: The process
body: The course follows a full product-development cycle on one product. Use the arrows to go through it.

items.title: From user needs to requirements
items.text: Market and user-review analysis gave 13 user needs, translated into 11 technical requirements: 2.4–3 kg, 60 min autonomy, about 200 air watts of suction, under 80 dB, a 1 L bin, cyclonic separation with a HEPA filter, recharge under 240 min and maximum footprints for the vacuum and its base.

items.alt: Hand sketches of concept solutions for the vacuum's subsystems
items.title: Functions and concepts
items.text: A black-box and modular breakdown split the product into subsystems; each one got several sketched concepts before choosing.

items.alt: Concept evolving into the first 3D models
items.title: From concept to 3D
items.text: The chosen layout became a first 3D model in Siemens NX, then the full product.

items.alt: CAD of the motor housing and impeller
items.title: Subsystem design
items.text: Each subsystem is traced back to the requirements it serves. The propulsion unit (ABS housing, steel impeller, 310 g) drives suction power and noise; the battery pack (340 g) is removable.

items.alt: Exploded view of the vacuum's main subsystems
items.title: Exploded assemblies
items.text: Exploded views of the main subsystems check assembly order and part count, from the motor stack to the cyclone and bin.

items.title: Production drawings
items.text: Dimensioned drawings for every major component, generated in NX.

items.alt: The vacuum standing in its charging base
items.title: Charging base
items.text: A vertical charging base stores the vacuum and accessories in a small footprint.

items.alt: Five color variants of the vacuum
items.title: Final design
items.text: The final assembly, with interchangeable colored shells as an attractiveness requirement.

items.alt: Digital human models using the vacuum in Tecnomatix
items.title: Ergonomic check
items.text: Digital human models in Tecnomatix scored the posture of right-handed and left-handed users, and of a bent posture, with RULA tables.
